summary: Confirmed DONE. The root cause is fixed. The Node HTTP server, which every remote runner uses (`node`, `ryco` and `npx` all run `dist/bin.mjs` with a `#!/usr/bin/env node` banner), now installs installHttpStartupGate before listen. The gate holds requests that arrive before HttpRouter.serve attaches and replays them through the newListener hook. @effect/platform-node attaches its handlers with server.on('request'/'upgrade'), so the hook fires. In serve (web) mode, `/` is deliberately not served early (isEarlyStaticAssetRequest), so wait_ready cannot report ready before the router serves. The defense-in-depth part also landed: the remote wait_ready per-probe timeout is now 250 ms (REMOTE_LOOPBACK_READY_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS), and the probe still accepts only 2xx, so the gate's 503 counts as not ready. I emulated it in memory, using the real httpStartupGate.ts module and the exact probe loop. Attach times were 145/200/280/600/1500/3000 ms and listen offsets 0/37/73 ms. Readiness lag after the router attaches was: old code (no gate, 1 s probe) min 335, median 851, max 1064 ms. Current code (gate, 250 ms probe) min 0, median 0, max 102 ms. An old remote `ryco` on PATH without the gate, probed at 250 ms, gives min 9, median 215, max 327 ms. The ~0.9 s penalty is gone. I found no real defect.

evidence.note: installHttpStartupGate(server) is called inside the NodeHttpServer.layer factory, so before listen. Node path only. Bun never blackholed.
Early handler: desktop mode serves the document, other modes serve only isEarlyStaticAssetRequest. So `/` (the wait_ready path) stays held until the router attaches (commit 347008e60).

newListener hook replays held requests and upgrades on nextTick once the real handlers attach. Held entries are dropped on response 'close', so a probe destroyed after 250 ms leaves no residue. Cap is 256 entries and 10 s, then 503 + Retry-After.

The platform attaches with server.on('request'/'upgrade'), so the gate's newListener detection works with the real serve path. Also covered by httpStartupGate.test.ts:182 ('startup gate with the Effect Node HTTP server').
`ryco serve` resolves mode to 'web' unless RYCO_MODE or a flag overrides it. So the non-desktop early-serve policy (`/` held) applies to the SSH remote.
REMOTE_LOOPBACK_READY_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS = 250. Old code substituted SSH_READY_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS (1000) at the old :543.
RYCO_READY_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS now takes the 250 ms constant. It feeds wait_ready (:382-383) for the cold launch (:474) and both reuse checks (:415-451).
Probe uses http.get timeout = probeTimeoutMs and resolves true only for 2xx, followed by a 100 ms sleep. A 503 from the gate counts as not ready.

The runner prefers a `ryco` already on the remote PATH. An older global install without the gate still blackholes during its dead window, but the 250 ms timeout caps that at ~330 ms (emulated) instead of ~1.06 s.
Pins the 250 ms value in the generated launch script.

The local tunnel waitForHttpReady keeps the 1 s default, which the finding did not ask to change. It runs after the remote is ready. OpenSSH binds -L listeners only after auth, so early local probes get ECONNREFUSED quickly and there is no dead window.

fixDefects: None verified. Notes on trade-offs, not defects: (1) Against a gated server, a 1 s probe timeout would give ~0 ms lag, because a held probe is almost always in flight at attach. With 250 ms plus a 100 ms sleep, about 100/350 of launches land in the sleep and lag up to ~100 ms (emulated max 102 ms). The 250 ms value buys the cap for old non-gated remote `ryco` installs. (2) The idle timeout covers the held time too, so a replayed probe must get headers within what is left of its 250 ms. On a slow, busy host right after attach it may be abandoned and retried. That is bounded by the 15 s deadline and costs at most a few 350 ms cycles. (3) The same 250 ms probe now drives the 2 s reuse checks (tunnel.ts:451), which kill a managed server that fails them. A healthy server whose `/` consistently takes 250-1000 ms would now be restarted where it was previously reused. That needs sustained event-loop stalls for about 2 s, so the risk is low.
implementationSketch: Optional micro-refinement, not required: in REMOTE_WAIT_READY_SCRIPT (packages/ssh/src/tunnel.ts:262-309), make probe() return 'refused' | 'timeout' | 'not-ok' | 'ok'. Re-probe right away after a 'timeout' (the server accepted the connection, so it is listening and the gate is holding or answering) and sleep 100 ms only after refused or non-2xx. That removes the up-to-100 ms lag against gated servers and keeps the 250 ms cap for non-gated old remotes. To harden the reuse path (:415-451), wait_ready could also take a per-call probe timeout (for example 1000 ms for REUSE checks, 250 ms for the cold launch), so a busy existing server is not killed. Test: extend tunnel.test.ts to assert the reuse call passes its own probe timeout, and add a small node-run test of the probe script against an http.Server with installHttpStartupGate attached after a delay. Assert readiness within about 10 ms of attach.
decisionReason: Done. The optional refinements are local to the SSH launch script and touch no auth, E2EE, Hub or hosted lifecycle semantics.
